markdown_report:
The best first architectural experiment is **content-conditioned forgetting inside GRU4Rec**, using learned item-ID embeddings and interaction order. It targets stale-interest revival and weak alignment with recent activity; improvement remains unproven.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users distinguish current usefulness from broad relevance; recent coherent activity supplies a plausible intent signal. (2) Electronics’ tenth-percentile margin is 0.0265 and negative-beats-positive rate is 9.7%; these indicate sampled confusion, not validation HR@10. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply near-zero mean cosine similarity, providing no evidence for global embedding diversification.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [TLSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) motivates memory gating, but timestamps cannot be recovered uniquely from item-only histories. (2) [T-GRU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) gates the carry term; whole-state pre-gating changes additional computations and needs separate validation. (3) [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) supports text sharing under pretraining, not necessarily randomly initialized encoders. (4) [GRU4Rec research](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847) makes loss/sampling strong practical alternatives.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Memory control addresses stale intent; representation sharing addresses sparse identity; objective design addresses confusing rankings. All remain within one jointly trained GRU network/category.

Scores denote originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; difficulty 10 means hardest. Each assessment includes a benefit and limitation.

| Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Content-conditioned forgetting | 4: constrained adaptation / established gating | 6: adaptive memory / uncertain incremental benefit | 8: stale and weak recent fit / compatibility unknown | 6: contextual separation / indirect effect | 4: small gate / recurrent and predictor integration |
| Shared trainable title encoder | 4: task adaptation / familiar fusion | 7: sparse transfer / weak supervision | 7: identifiable links / lexical shortcuts | 5: sparse discrimination / sparsity unmeasured | 6: compact encoder / vocabulary pipeline |
| Regularized BPR-max | 2: established / little novelty | 7: ranking gains / false negatives | 4: stronger distinctions / no intent mechanism | 9: targets weak margins / sampled proxy | 3: known objective / careful masking |

**Selected experiment.** Predict coordinate-wise retention from the current observed item embedding and previous hidden state; attenuate memory before the ordinary GRU update. This explicitly targets older-interest revival and broad matches displacing recent-intent matches, while potentially improving Electronics’ weak margins. It cannot establish ownership, compatibility, mood, or concrete purpose.

Set added weights to zero and bias to logit(0.99), giving initial retention 0.99; this is not identity and compounds across steps. Compare corrected GRU, fixed retention=1, learned pre-gating, carry-only gating, and an actively used parameter-matched control. Hold baseline loss/sampling fixed; defer text and objective changes. Temporal variants require occurrence-aligned inputs at both training and inference and are excluded under item-only inference.

Predeclare this bounded comparison within 43,200 GPU-seconds, recording failures. Preserve four routes, seeds 0/42, ≤200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch, matching predictors and diagnostics. Skip padding; read the final nonpadding position. Track gate saturation and cumulative log-retention. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10; report paired within-category user-bootstrap uncertainty when hit indicators are available. Repeated selection remains optimistic, and sampled rankings need not generalize to full catalogs ([sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [selection bias](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

idea.description: Add a coordinate-wise retention gate before each ordinary recurrent update of the corrected GRU4Rec. The gate uses only the current observed item's jointly learned ID embedding and the previous hidden state. 'Content-conditioned' therefore means embedding-conditioned, not text-conditioned. Train one independent network per category, selecting one checkpoint per category without score fusion or checkpoint averaging.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies older-interest revival and broadly related items displacing stronger recent-intent matches. Conditional attenuation directly intervenes on memory persistence and is eligible because it explicitly addresses both failures. Electronics’ 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin, 9.7% negative-beats-positive rate, and 14.82% small-margin rate supply a model-facing target. However, attenuation may discard useful persistent interests, and sampled margins do not establish validation performance. BPR-max is a strong practical alternative, but alone lacks a direct mechanism for the two required user-facing failures. At 0% research progress, a small controlled architectural experiment is preferable to combining temporal, textual, and objective changes.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the corrected family-specific baseline, including hidden size, embedding sharing, ordinary GRU equations, loss, negative sampler, optimizer, dropout, batch size and checkpoint-selection schedule. The supplied report does not include their numeric values; inherit them from the host baseline and record them in the trial configuration rather than inventing replacements. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all artifacts stay beneath the trial directory. Preserve all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, a maximum of 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Execute each trial on one GPU and count training, diagnostics, debugging and failures against 43,200 GPU-seconds.

For embedding dimension d and hidden dimension H, define retention r_t = sigmoid(W_x x_t + W_h h_previous + b), with W_x shaped H×d and W_h shaped H×H. Initialize both matrices to zero and every bias to log(99), giving r_t=0.99 initially. This adds H(d+H+1) parameters. Finite sigmoid bias does not give exact identity; the direct additional retention factor is initially 0.99^k across k valid steps, before ordinary GRU effects. Zero weight initialization makes the initial gate constant, although gate parameters can receive gradients. Monitor saturation because a near-one sigmoid has a small derivative.

Use order-based inputs throughout. Do not construct item-to-time dictionaries or infer occurrence timestamps from truncated item histories: identical item sequences can have different event times. A temporal extension is admissible only if occurrence-aligned timestamps can be sliced and padded together with items and are available unambiguously at inference. Its gaps must involve already observed events; the first retained gap is unknown unless its predecessor is available. Fit normalization on training events only, never use target timestamps, and exercise any missing-time pathway during training. Under the stated item-only compatibility interface, exclude this extension from the proposed comparison.

Predeclare five configurations: corrected baseline, fixed r=1 implementation check, learned whole-state pre-gate, learned carry-only gate, and an actively used parameter-matched control. For the control, compute a_t=tanh(A_x x_t+A_h h_previous+c) and pass h_previous+0.1*a_t to the ordinary GRU, using the same added parameter count, zero weights and zero bias initially. It starts at the baseline and tests an additional recurrent transformation without multiplicative attenuation; it cannot isolate every optimization difference. For carry-only gating, preserve the baseline candidate/reset computation and multiply only its existing carry term by r_t, respecting the baseline's update-gate convention. The fixed-r=1 configuration should reproduce baseline outputs and gradients before spending a full training run; floating-point differences from a changed execution path must be checked. Run the baseline and pre-gate first, then remaining controls only within a predeclared compute allocation. If controls cannot fit, report them as unrun and restrict causal claims. Defer loss/sampling and text experiments to avoid confounding this first comparison.

Mask padding explicitly: padding leaves recurrent state unchanged, diagnostic features at padded positions are zero, and loss includes only valid supervised positions. Read the largest nonpadding index, never count-1 on left-padded input. Handle all-padding inputs using the host baseline's defined fallback. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), their shapes and scoring behavior. Each checkpoint must contain architecture variant, dimensions, initialization configuration and state_dict. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical architecture and verify scores agree with the in-memory selected model on identical histories and candidates. Each category loads exactly one selected checkpoint.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; train_loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B×L. Preserve existing valid-position sampled-margin probes and definitions. Add measured retention quantiles, fraction below 0.01 or above 0.99, and per-coordinate sums of log retention across valid positions, summarized by history-length bins 1–5, 6–10, 11–20 and >20. A temporary diagnostic hook can collect internal gates without changing log2feats return values. Time-gap stratification is unavailable in this item-only experiment. Keep diagnosis batches fixed across variants and separate these training-history diagnostics from validation evidence. Category breakdowns should be marked unavailable when item category metadata is absent, rather than invented. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; review text/ratings, item categories/prices/stores/ratings, simulator traits, and true compatibility are unavailable.

Select by the unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. If the host exposes per-user hit indicators, retain paired baseline/challenger outcomes and use 10,000 bootstrap resamples with analysis seed 42, sampling 200 users with replacement independently within each category and sharing sampled indices between models. Report the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of macro HR differences. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on candidates and trained checkpoints; they exclude seed variation and do not correct adaptive selection. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain missing outputs or invent intervals. Preserve the native five training-user full-catalog recommendations per category, but do not equate their qualitative findings with sampled validation gains. Limit claims to measured benchmark behavior; no test access, external weights, additional datasets, other-trial checkpoints or independently fitted scoring components.
idea.pseudocode:
For each predeclared variant, train categories independently using the host baseline:
  set preprocessing seed=0 and training seed=42
  inherit and record all corrected baseline hyperparameters
  initialize ordinary GRU4Rec
  if variant is learned pre-gate or carry-only:
    W_x=0; W_h=0; bias=log(99)
  if variant is additive capacity control:
    A_x=0; A_h=0; c=0
  for epoch in range(at_most_200):
    for batch_index in range(200):
      _, sequence, positive, negative = baseline_sample_batch()
      h = zeros
      for t in chronological sequence positions:
        valid = sequence[:, t] != 0
        x = baseline_item_input(sequence[:, t])
        if variant is baseline or fixed_retention_one:
          proposed = baseline_GRU_update(x, h)
        elif variant is learned_pre_gate:
          r = sigmoid(W_x*x + W_h*h + bias)
          proposed = baseline_GRU_update(x, r*h)
        elif variant is learned_carry_only:
          r = sigmoid(W_x*x + W_h*h + bias)
          carry, candidate = baseline_GRU_terms(x, h)
          proposed = carry*r*h + (1-carry)*candidate
        elif variant is additive_capacity_control:
          a = tanh(A_x*x + A_h*h + c)
          proposed = baseline_GRU_update(x, h + 0.1*a)
        h = where(valid, proposed, h)
        features[:, t] = where(valid, h, 0)
      loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative, valid_positions)
      optimize_all_parameters_jointly(loss)
    apply_unchanged_host_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
  save_one_selected_checkpoint_per_category_with_architecture_configuration()
  write_matching_embedded_predictor()
  run_fixed_diagnostic_batches_and_record_compute()
At inference:
  reconstruct the selected architecture from its category checkpoint
  compute causal features from item IDs only, skipping padding updates
  last_index = maximum position whose item ID is nonzero
  use host fallback if no valid position exists
  score candidates using the existing learned scoring function
Compare configurations using the pinned macro validation HR@10; never combine their predictions.

originality.positive: The constrained adaptation explicitly tests whole-state, embedding-conditioned attenuation against carry-only gating and an equal-parameter recurrent control.
originality.negative: Recurrent gates and temporal retention mechanisms are established; omitting timestamps makes this closer to an additional conventional learned gate than a new temporal model.

future_potential.positive: Controlled results could clarify whether additional memory attenuation helps order-only GRU recommendation and identify destructive retention patterns.
future_potential.negative: The ordinary GRU already learns forgetting, and item-only attenuation cannot establish current purpose, ownership redundancy or equipment compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The core experiment adds two small projections and a bias without new data pipelines or external weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Custom recurrent execution, faithful carry-only controls, diagnostic hooks and exact checkpoint/predictor agreement require careful integration and may reduce training throughput.

related_work.title: TLSRec (2022)
contributions: Motivates learned temporal gating between long- and short-term preferences.
limitations: Does not establish gains under the pinned Amazon GRU4Rec protocol.
Historical elapsed time requires occurrence-aligned inputs, and inactivity alone does not establish changed intent.

related_work.title: T-GRU / MTAM
contributions: Provides a close recommendation precedent for gating the recurrent carry term using elapsed time, input and history.
Motivates distinguishing carry-only retention from whole-state pre-gating.
limitations: Its reported results do not establish benefits for the proposed whole-state pre-gate or parameter-matched superiority.
Its temporal inputs are unavailable under item-only inference.

related_work.title: TiSASRec
contributions: Models historical time intervals alongside sequence positions with explicit temporal inputs.
limitations: Uses a different backbone and serves here as an input-alignment reference.
Item IDs alone cannot reconstruct occurrence-specific elapsed times.

related_work.title: Recformer (KDD 2023)
contributions: Supports item-text representation learning for sparse and cold-start recommendation.
limitations: Uses a pretrained Transformer outside the required backbone and permitted weight sources.
Its results do not establish gains for a randomly initialized compact text encoder.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec
contributions: Provides recurrent recommendation methods and practical BPR-max and sampled-cross-entropy objectives.
limitations: Objective and sampling recommendations require validation under the pinned protocol.
Hard-negative emphasis can amplify false-negative supervision.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Establishes loss functions and negative sampling as consequential choices for recurrent recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed attenuation mechanism improves Amazon macro validation HR@10.

related_work.title: Can Recurrent Neural Networks Warp Time? — Chrono Initialization
contributions: Motivates initializing recurrent gate biases with explicit memory timescales.
limitations: Does not justify a particular retention probability for this benchmark.
Near-saturated gates can learn slowly; the proposed 0.99 initialization remains an experimental choice.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce conclusions inconsistent with full-catalog metrics.
limitations: Does not replace or authorize changes to the pinned evaluator.
Validation conclusions must remain conditional on the supplied candidate protocol.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how adaptive model selection can overfit finite validation criteria.
limitations: A bounded search reduces exposure but does not eliminate selection bias.
Conditional bootstrap intervals do not correct repeated checkpoint or configuration selection.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a paired-bootstrap precedent adapted here to within-category user resampling.
limitations: This application is a methodological adaptation to recommendation hit indicators.
It requires exposed per-user outcomes and measures neither training-seed nor candidate-sampling uncertainty.
